text: The project owner chose a red dot on the tab icon (favicon-turn.svg) as the only 'your turn' signal. Options considered and turned down: changing the tab title (owner preferred the icon), browser notifications (permission prompt, more code), sound (autoplay limits, annoying). No signal at game end was a deliberate YAGNI choice. The icon is the tall light round solid piece; it is not in misc/Quarto.html, so the owner may add it to the design later. Revisit notifications only if the icon proves too easy to miss.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The light/dark/auto theme button at the top right is not in misc/Quarto.html. The owner asked for it on 2026-11-18 after the design's dark mode was built; the design itself says only to follow the system setting. Do not remove the button to match the design. The owner chose one button that cycles Auto, Light, Dark over a three-part control, and chose to line it up with the room top bar rather than the page corner. Below 390px the room bar spacing is tighter than the design so that the button fits.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The game screen is longer than the visible area on phones (about 838px of content at 390px wide against about 660px visible), so it scrolls during play. The owner chose to accept this scroll on 2026-11-17 and gave no reason. Two alternatives were offered and not chosen. One was a shorter phone layout, which changes the reference design in misc/Quarto.html (that design draws the phone as a 390x844 frame with no browser bars). The other was a board that scales to the viewport height, which makes the squares smaller than the 44px touch size. Do not treat this scroll as a bug.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The game is installable to a phone home screen through manifest.webmanifest and PNG icons only (added 2026-11-18). The owner approved three limits; do not treat them as oversights. (1) No service worker and no offline cache: the game cannot be played offline, and with no build step there is no automatic cache version, so a cached page could stay on a phone after a deploy. With no network the installed app shows the browser error page. (2) On iOS a home screen app has its own storage and room links from a chat open in Safari, so an invited iOS player plays in Safari and the installed app does not know their name, seat or last room. The owner accepted this. A 'join by code' field in the lobby was offered and not built: it is not in the design and it cannot restore a seat taken in Safari; the code review raised it again as the only way to enter a new invitation inside the installed app. (3) The app icon is one piece (the owner's favicon.svg piece) on the light linen background, not the four lobby pieces; the owner supplied the favicon in answer to the icon question. The manifest colours are static, so the splash screen is light also for dark-theme players. The PNG files were rendered from icon.svg with headless Chrome at each size (ImageMagick dropped the SVG strokes); render them again by hand if icon.svg changes.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The project owner wanted a per-room win count, shown next to the player names (2026-11-18). 'New game' during a game was replaced by 'Forfeit', which gives the win to the other player, because otherwise a player who sees they will lose can restart to avoid the loss. On an empty game the button stays 'New game' with no score change, so players can still restart to let the other one start. Decided with the owner: only wins count, not draws; no reset button (a new room starts at 0-0); the score is per seat in one room, not per person across rooms; no designer frame was made first, so the score in the chips is not in misc/Quarto.html. Rejected: a forfeit button that adds the win and clears the board at once (the opponent sees the board clear with no reason), and storing a list of past games (grows without limit for no gain).
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Rule choices made by the project owner, with the options that were turned down. (1) A player must call Quarto; the page does not detect a win by itself. Automatic detection was offered as the simpler option and was refused, because the owner wants the official rule where a player can miss a line. (2) A wrong call has no penalty. 'A wrong call loses' and 'one free wrong call per game' were offered and refused; the owner accepts that a player can press the button after each move, as in the physical game. (3) Undo removes only the player's own last action, until the opponent acts. 'Any player at any time' and 'the opponent must approve' were refused. The owner knows and accepts that this lets a player who gave a piece and then sees their own missed line undo and call it, if the opponent has not acted yet. Do not 'fix' this as a loophole. (4) No 2x2 square variant.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The designer's reference design is misc/Quarto.html, and the page is built from it. The file is a packed export: the root page holds a JSON manifest (base64, gzip) of 38 nested pages, and each nested page is again a manifest plus a template; unpack both levels to read the frames. The page differs from the frames in these places ON PURPOSE; do not 'correct' the page to match them. (1) While the page is not connected, every game control is off, 'New game' included; the frames leave 'New game' on. The owner decided that play stops when the connection is lost. (2) 'Undo' is on during the opponent's turn when the last action is the player's own; the 'opponent's turn' frame shows it off, which is against the rules the owner chose. In general the rules in game.js decide which control is on, and the design gives only the look. (3) The design gives no time for when a short connection loss becomes the 'Connection lost' notice; the owner accepted about 5 seconds. Font history: the first design used Figtree, which has no Greek letters; players type names in Greek, so the designer and the owner replaced it fully with Commissioner. The Cyrillic and Vietnamese subsets that the design file also contains were left out on purpose. Wording: the owner chose the designer's wording over the first version's strings; strings for states that have no frame were written to match it.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The lobby install message (added 2026-11-18) is not in misc/Quarto.html; the owner asked for 'a prompt on first launch to install to the home screen' and approved this form. Do not remove it to match the design. Decisions the owner approved: (1) Lobby only, never in a room and never a pop-up. A pop-up at first launch was rejected: it interrupts a player who is joining a game, and on Android it is not possible, because Chrome fires beforeinstallprompt only after one tap and 30 seconds on the site in total, so the message can appear late or only on a later lobby visit. On iOS an install from inside a room would lose that room, because the installed app has its own storage. (2) iPhone and iPad players get instruction text only, found by user agent sniffing; in-app browsers show it although they cannot install. (3) The message also shows in desktop Chrome and Edge with the 'home screen' wording, because that costs no code. (4) The page always calls preventDefault on beforeinstallprompt, in rooms too, so the lobby message is the only install promotion and a player who selected 'Not now' does not get the browser bar in its place. (5) 'Not now' is permanent (localStorage quarto.installDismissed); a cancel in the system install dialog is not. Firefox on Android shows nothing. Open point: the installed app cannot open a new invitation (no address bar, and no 'Join game' field in the lobby); a join field was recommended as a separate ticket and the owner has not decided.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Firefox showed 'Connection lost' for about 30 seconds after each connect, because Firefox fetch resolves only at the first body byte and Gweet sent nothing until its 30-second keepalive. The owner fixed this in Gweet (commit ff06d79 in skorokithakis/gweet): the stream now sends one keepalive newline as soon as the subscription is registered, to ALL clients. Rejected: (1) an opt-in query parameter for the early newline, which would protect existing Gweet clients that read only the first line or treat any byte as a message; the owner accepted that risk. (2) A Quarto-only fix that shows 'Connected' before the stream response arrives, because it can show 'Connected' while no updates arrive, against the rule that play stops when the connection is lost. (3) A longer 'Connection lost' delay, because it hides the symptom.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: The project owner chose online play through Gweet (their own HTTP message queue, server https://gweet.stavros.io) over two other options: play on one shared device, and peer-to-peer WebRTC. Play on one shared device is an explicit non-goal, not an oversight. Protection against cheating is also an explicit non-goal: any person with the room link can write any state, and the owner accepts this for games between friends. When two players act at the same moment, last write wins and one action is lost; the owner accepted this in place of a fair tie-break.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
